doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

chapter: Basie alumni and childhood in Hollis
title: Jo Jones and Al Hibbler teach him to listen
summary: Jo Jones and Hibbler gave him records to identify within a week.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I’ve never found it again. I’d like to have it. And let’s not leave out Jo Jones, the original, the babysitter, you know I was going to Jo Jones’ apartment learning jazz lessons from Jo Jones, it’s a tough struggle, but I knew him and he was great.
What kinds of things did he teach you?

How to listen to records so you didn’t say something stupid. That’s an important lesson. Him and Al Hibbler. Say, “Monk, who do you think’s playing alto on this record?” And you’d say, “Well I don’t know.” “You can’t tell, Monk?” “No I can’t.” “Well tell you what. Here’s the record. Listen to it for a week. Come back next Saturday morning. But if you can’t tell me next Saturday morning give me back the record and don’t come here no more.” Now that’s a tough teaching — their method. I hope I’m not that mean. But they weren’t mean to me.
